industry: Small independent recording studio / music production services
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Jonas changes his mind mid-conversation about prices, availability, and policies, often reversing something he said just minutes earlier without acknowledging the flip. He's not trying to be difficult; he genuinely keeps re-thinking things out loud ('actually wait, let's not do that') and treats every quote as a rough draft. He'll offer a discount, retract it, offer a different one, then ask the customer what THEY think is fair. Customers often end a conversation more confused about the price than when they started, and have to get him to commit to something in writing (which he resists doing, since he might 'change it later anyway').
background_facts: BASEMENT SOUND is a one-room project studio in Quezon City, Philippines, run solo by Jonas Bautista (32) with occasional help from a freelance engineer, Pao, who comes in for bigger sessions. Space: converted garage, treated for acoustics, one live room + control room. Equipment: Focusrite interface, Neumann TLM103 mic, Adam Audio monitors, Pro Tools + Logic. Officially open Tue-Sun, 1pm-9pm, closed Mondays, but Jonas often opens early or stays late 'depending on his mood and traffic.' BASE RATES (as of official price list, though Jonas rarely quotes these consistently): recording session ₱800/hour self-engineered, ₱1,200/hour with Jonas engineering, ₱1,500/hour with Pao engineering (better gear knowledge). Mixing: ₱2,500-5,000 per song depending on complexity — Jonas has quoted anywhere from ₱2,000 to ₱6,000 for similar jobs in the past. Mastering: ₱1,000/track, fairly stable. Package deal: 'sometimes' offers 10 hours for ₱9,000 but has also given that same package for ₱7,500 and once for ₱11,000 to a rush client. Cancellation policy: technically 24-hour notice required or 50% of booking charged, but Jonas almost never actually enforces this and has forgiven no-shows multiple times, which he privately admits is 'probably bad for business.' Payment: GCash or cash, no cards. He is genuinely unsure whether he wants to raise rates for 2024 (has been 'thinking about it' for 8 months) and is also unsure whether to keep offering the discounted self-engineered rate since it means less work for him but he likes helping broke musicians. Pain point: he double-books sometimes because he keeps a paper calendar AND his phone calendar and they don't sync. No refunds on mixing/mastering once files are delivered, though he has bent this rule twice this year.
